title: OTWD fact values
description: The value shapes of every fact a record can carry, for sites, road restrictions, road segments and ferry services. The full form wraps each value with its provenance (common.schema.json#/$defs/Fact). A submission proposes bare values, and OTWD adds provenance when the change is applied. Values that more than one record type uses, such as names, opening hours, weight limits and seasonal closures, are defined once here. This file defines no document of its own.

Names.description: The names a site is known by. Exactly one entry has kind primary.

kind.description: primary: the name shown by default. alternative: another current name. traditional: a name in the language of the traditional owners or First Nations people of the area. former: a name no longer used. short: an abbreviation.

Coordinates.description: A latitude and longitude in WGS84 (EPSG:4326), in decimal degrees, with an optional accuracy. Location and SiteLocation build on it and close the object.

Location.description: The coordinates of a road restriction: the point on the road where the limit applies, such as the centre of the road under a bridge. Always exact, because a road restriction's location is a safety fact.

SiteLocation.description: The coordinates of a site. For a large site such as a campground this is the entrance or office, where a traveller would drive to. When the site has a location_sensitivity fact, the published coordinates are generalised (ADR 0045): lat and lng are rounded to the nearest multiple of generalised.cell_deg and accuracy_m is left out, so they name a grid cell rather than the place. Submissions always carry the exact position and never generalised.

Generalisation.description: How a published site position was generalised. cell_deg: the grid cell size in degrees, 0.01 (about 1.1 km north to south), 0.1 (about 11 km) or 1 (about 111 km). lat and lng are rounded to the nearest multiple of it, which tools/validate.py checks.

SiteTypes.description: The site's primary site type and any others it also serves as. A showground that is also a dump point has primary showground and others [dump_point].

Description.description: A short original description of the site, at most one per language, each in the language its contributor wrote it in. It must be the contributor's own words, never copied from a website, guidebook or other database, and never a machine translation of another description.

OpeningHours.description: When a site can be used or a ferry service runs. Times and dates are local clock times and local calendar dates, read in the record's time zone or in time_zone when it is given, and never converted to UTC. Give always_open, a weekly pattern, an OSM opening_hours string, or a combination. When both weekly and osm_opening_hours are present they describe the same hours and weekly is authoritative.

always_open.description: True for a site open 24 hours a day every day, such as most rest areas.

weekly.description: The regular weekly pattern. Days with no entry are closed, unless always_open is true.

closes.description: Closing time. A closing time earlier than the opening time means the period ends after midnight.

osm_opening_hours.description: The same hours in OpenStreetMap opening_hours syntax, for example "Mo-Fr 08:00-17:00; Sa 09:00-12:00". Accepted from contributors who already write in that syntax.

exceptions.description: Dates that differ from the weekly pattern, such as public holidays.

seasonal_closures.description: Periods the site closes every year, such as a wet season closure.

ScheduleTimeZone.description: The IANA time zone this schedule's local times and dates are read in, when it differs from the record's time_zone, for example when a track starts in one state but the authority in another closes it, or a ferry keeps the clock of the terminal at the far end for its hours or its fare seasons. It must be one of the zones the record lies in (time_zones for a line). Leave it out when the record's time_zone applies.

AnnualPeriod.description: A period that repeats every year, from one local calendar day to another inclusive, read in the record's time zone or the schedule's own time_zone. A period may wrap past the end of the year, for example 11-01 to 03-31.

AuthorityLink.description: The authority that sets a rule or issues a notice, and its official information page. The record that uses it says which of the two it requires and what the page covers.

authority.description: The authority or land manager, as it names itself, for example Parks Victoria.

info_url.description: The authority's official page for the rule, the notice or current conditions.

Prices.description: What it costs to use the site. charging says whether there is a charge at all. items lists the prices.

charging.description: free: no charge. donation: a voluntary payment is invited. paid: a charge applies and items lists it.

PriceItem.description: One price. The amount is charged per unit (per) for each period, so per person per night is per=person, period=night.

applies_to.description: What is being paid for. Use other with notes when none fits. Open: a consumer that does not know the value shows the price as other.

per.description: The unit the amount is charged per. Open: a consumer that does not know the unit shows the amount without working out a total.

period.description: The period the amount covers. Open, with the same fallback as per.

MoneyAmount.description: Amount in major currency units, for example 32.5 for A$32.50.

ChargePeriod.description: The period a price or fee is charged for: per night, day, hour, week, stay or use (one crossing or one visit). Open: a consumer that does not know the period shows the amount without working out a total.

PaymentMethods.description: How a price or fare can be paid. Open: a consumer ignores a method it does not know.

PriceConditions.description: When a price applies. All given conditions must hold.

concession.description: True when the price applies only to holders of a concession, seniors or pensioner card.

FireDistrict.description: Safety fact. The fire authority and fire district the site falls in, with a link to the authority's official live fire ban information. OTWD never stores declared fire bans: they change daily, so apps send travellers to ban_info_url.

authority.description: The fire authority's name, for example Country Fire Authority.

district.description: The fire district, fire area or total fire ban district as the authority names it, for example North Central.

ban_info_url.description: The authority's official page for current fire bans and fire danger ratings in this district.

RigLimits.description: Safety fact. Limits on which vehicles can use the site. A limit that is absent is unknown, not unlimited.

max_length_m.description: Longest total rig, vehicle plus anything towed, that fits, in metres.

max_height_m.description: Lowest overhead clearance on the way in or on site, in metres.

max_weight_t.description: Lowest gross mass limit on the way in, such as a bridge or causeway limit, in tonnes.

big_rig_suitable.description: yes: room to enter, turn and park a big rig (roughly 10 m or more combined, or a large motorhome). limited: possible with care or only on some sites. no: unsuitable.

towing_allowed.description: False when caravans, camper trailers and other towed vehicles are not allowed.

Access.description: Safety fact. How a vehicle reaches the site.

road_surface.description: The worst surface on the last stretch to the site. The codes other than mixed are the same as in the surface governed list (surfaces.json).

unsealed_km.description: Length of unsealed road from the nearest sealed road, in kilometres.

SeasonalAccess.description: Whether access depends on the season or the weather.

wet_weather_closure.description: True when the road closes or becomes impassable after rain.

Pets.description: The site's pet policy. allowed is the general rule for pets. species gives the rule for each species where it differs or is known, and allowed must not be no when any species is allowed. The facilities pets_allowed and dog_off_leash are read from this fact.

PetAllowed.description: yes: pets allowed. on_leash: allowed on a leash at all times. by_arrangement: only with prior approval. no: not allowed (assistance animals are covered by law, not by this field).

PetSpeciesRule.description: The rule for one species, from the pet species governed list (pet-species.json), with the same values as pets.allowed (PetAllowed). max_number is the most of that species per pitch or booking.

PetConditions.description: Conditions on pets that are allowed. areas says where pets may stay: whole_site anywhere on the site, designated_pitches only on the pitches set aside for pets, all_pitches on any pitch but not in cabins, cabins only in pet-friendly cabins, day_use_area only in the day use area. not_allowed_periods are periods each year, as local month and day, when pets are not allowed, such as the summer school holidays.

max_pets.description: Most pets per pitch or booking, of all species together.

PetFee.description: A charge per pet in the shared money shape: amount (MoneyAmount) and currency as in a price item, for each period from ChargePeriod, such as A$10 per pet per night, or per crossing (use) on a ferry service.

FerryPetPolicy.description: How a ferry service carries pets. carried no: pets are not carried. carried yes: pets travel in one or more arrangements. in_vehicle: the pet stays in the traveller's vehicle on the vehicle deck. kennel: in a kennel on board. pet_friendly_cabin: in a cabin set aside for pets and their owners. on_deck_on_leash: on an open deck on a leash. in_carrier: in a closed carrier in the passenger areas. Assistance animals are covered by law, not by this fact.

species.description: The species this arrangement takes. Absent means every species the operator carries.

PetTransit.description: Whether travellers may take pets along a road segment, such as a road through a national park. yes: allowed. in_vehicle_only: allowed in transit if the pet stays in the vehicle. no: not allowed even in a vehicle. The authority that sets the rule and its information page are required, because the rule is the authority's to change. info_url is the authority's page for its rules on pets.

species.description: The species the rule applies to. Absent means every pet.

BaitNotices.description: Safety fact. Notices that poison baits for pest animals, such as 1080 (sodium fluoroacetate) or PAPP baits, are laid in or next to the site or road segment. A bait can kill a dog that finds it. OTWD records the notice as signed or published, with its area, local dates and the authority's link, and never the authority's live baiting programme: apps send travellers to info_url for current baiting.

BaitNotice.description: One bait notice. from and to are local dates as the notice gives them, read in the record's time zone or in time_zone when it is given. A notice with no to stays until the authority withdraws it. authority is the authority or land manager running the baiting, and info_url its page for current baiting programmes.

area.description: The area baited, as the notice describes it, for example the reserve north of the campground.

poison.description: The poison named on the notice, for example 1080.

CampingRules.description: Whether a traveller may camp overnight at a site or along a road segment, under the rules of the council or land manager that sets them (ADR 0043). OTWD records the standing rule as the authority publishes or signs it, with the authority and its page for the rules, and never enforcement or day-to-day closures. allowed: camping is allowed, with no conditions beyond those recorded here and in stay_limits. restricted: allowed only under conditions, such as only in marked bays, only in certified self-contained vehicles or only with a permit. prohibited: no overnight camping. A missing fact is unknown, never proof that camping is allowed.

SelfContainedRequirement.description: Whether only self-contained vehicles may camp, and the certification schemes the authority accepts, from the self-contained scheme governed list (self-contained-schemes.json). required true: only a vehicle certified under one of schemes may camp, so camping must be restricted. schemes absent with required true: the authority asks for a self-contained vehicle without naming a scheme. Each scheme must be used in the record's country.

Permits.description: The permits a traveller needs to enter, camp at or travel through a site or road segment (ADR 0043). OTWD records that a permit is needed, who issues it and where to get it, never a traveller's permit.

Permit.description: One permit, with the authority that issues it and its page for applying. kind park_entry: a pass to enter a park or reserve. camping: a permit or booking that camping requires. land_entry: a permit to enter land held by its traditional owners or a community, such as Aboriginal land in the Northern Territory. transit: a permit to travel along a road through such land or a reserve, keeping to the road. other: any other permit, described in notes. in_advance true: the permit must be obtained before arrival, not at the site or on the way. free true: the authority issues it without charge.

QuietHours.description: The site's quiet hours as its rules or signs give them: local clock times read in the site's time zone, never converted to UTC. A to earlier than from means the period ends after midnight. days limits them to some days of the week, and absent means every day.

AgeRules.description: Who the site takes by age. children_allowed false: the site takes adults only, and min_guest_age is the age from which it takes a guest, such as 18. min_booking_age: the age the person who books or registers must be, such as 18 or 25, whether or not children are allowed.

Firewood.description: Firewood at the site. for_sale true: the operator sells firewood on site. provided true: the operator supplies it at no extra charge. collection: whether travellers may gather firewood on or around the site: allowed, restricted (only fallen dead wood, or only in some areas, as notes say) or prohibited. Whether fires are allowed at all is the fires_allowed facility.

TidalAccess.description: Safety fact. Reaching the site or driving the road segment depends on the tide, such as a beach drive or a crossing covered at high tide (ADR 0043). OTWD records the standing rule and the tide authority's prediction page in authority and info_url, never live tides or tide times: apps send travellers to info_url for the tides on the day. low_tide_window_h: the hours either side of low tide in which the authority or the signs advise travelling, when they give one. station: the tide station the advice refers to, as the authority names it. time_zone works as on a bait notice, for a road segment that crosses zones.

SeasonalOperation.description: The periods each year a site operates, as local month and day read in the site's time zone, such as a caravan park open from April to October (ADR 0043). It is the site's own season, distinct from a seasonal closure, which an authority declares, and from a temporary closure. Outside every period the site is not operating. A site gives its season here or as opening_hours.seasonal_closures, never both. dates_year: the year whose published dates the periods came from, when the operator sets them each year.

WaterNotices.description: Safety fact. Notices from a water authority or health department that the water supply at a site is not safe to drink as supplied (ADR 0044). OTWD records each notice as the authority published it, with the affected area, local dates and the authority's page, never a live water quality feed: apps send travellers to info_url for the current advice. Apps that show the drinking_water facility show current water notices beside it.

WaterNotice.description: One water notice. kind boil_water: boil the water before drinking it or using it for food. do_not_drink: do not drink the water even after boiling, though it may serve other uses as the notice says. do_not_use: do not use the water at all. other: any other water quality advice, described in notes. from and to are local dates as the notice gives them, read in the site's time zone. A notice with no to stays until the authority lifts it. authority is the authority that issued it and info_url its page for the notice or current notices.

area.description: The area or supply the notice covers, as it describes them, for example the town supply of Example Creek.

FloodDepthMarker.description: Safety fact. Whether a depth marker (a depth indicator post graduated in metres) stands at a ford or causeway so travellers can read the depth of water over the road, and the road authority with its page for current road conditions (ADR 0044). OTWD records the marker, never a live depth: water rises and falls by the hour, so apps send travellers to info_url and to the marker itself. present false: the crossing has no marker, so the depth cannot be read on site.

LocationSensitivity.description: The site's exact position must not be published, and why (ADR 0045). reason comes from the location sensitivity reason governed list (location-sensitivity-reasons.json). A moderator sets it, and the site's published location is then generalised to a grid cell at least as coarse as the reason's min_cell_deg, without accuracy_m, and the site has no locality. The exact position is held privately for moderation and never appears in the API, bulk downloads or the change feed. It carries no free text, so nothing about the place or the request is published beyond the reason.

review_on.description: The local date on which moderators review whether the marking is still needed, when one is set. A marking for cultural_heritage is reviewed only with the people who asked for it.

AccessFeature.description: Wheelchair access to one feature. yes: a wheelchair user can reach and use it without help. limited: usable with help or with difficulty, such as a ramp steeper than the standard allows or a door narrower than a modern chair. no: a wheelchair user cannot reach or use it. notes says what limits it.

WheelchairAccess.description: Wheelchair access, as in OSM wheelchair=*: yes, limited or no. AccessFeature describes each value.

SiteAccessFeature.description: A feature of a site whose wheelchair access is recorded. arrival: the entrance, reception or the point where a traveller arrives. pitches: the pitches, the individual camping spots for one rig or tent. camp_kitchen: the camp kitchen. The rest are the toilets, showers, parking, paths between the features and cabins.

AccessibilityBasis.description: What the accessibility fact rests on, alongside its provenance. assessed_to_standard: assessed against a named access standard, given in standard, such as AS 1428.1 in Australia. signposted: the operator or land manager signs the features as accessible, for example with the International Symbol of Access. operator_reported: stated by the operator or land manager, or a seed source, without a named standard. contributor_observation: what a contributor saw or used on site.

standard.description: The standard assessed against, as its publisher names it, for example AS 1428.1-2021.

assessed_on.description: The local date of the assessment.

AccessibleToilets.description: Toilets for people with disability. accessible_count counts wheelchair accessible toilets and ambulant_count toilets with grab rails for people who walk with difficulty, recorded only when someone counted them: a count of 0 records that there are none. A source that only says whether there is an accessible toilet sets wheelchair.toilets, and one that only says whether there is an ambulant toilet sets ambulant, never a count. changing_places is true when there is a Changing Places toilet, with a hoist and an adult change table. key_scheme names the central key that opens the toilets, from the key scheme governed list (key-schemes.json), and must be a scheme used in the site's country.

ambulant.description: True when there is at least one ambulant toilet, false when there is none. It must agree with ambulant_count when both are given.

key_required.description: True when a key is needed, from a key scheme or from the operator.

AccessiblePaths.description: The paths between the accessible features: the main path surface and notes on gradient, such as a steep ramp to the amenities block. path_surface has its own values, chosen for wheelchairs: they are not the surface governed list (surfaces.json), which describes roads and shares only sealed and sand with it.

SiteAccessibility.description: Access for people with disability at a site. wheelchair gives yes, limited or no per feature. basis says what the fact rests on. The accessible_facilities facility is read from this fact. A change that raises access to yes goes to a person (the accessibility_raised fixed check), because a wrong yes can strand a traveller who relied on it.

wheelchair.description: Wheelchair access to each feature of the site, keyed by SiteAccessFeature. A feature that is absent is unknown.

accessible_parking_spaces.description: Parking spaces marked for people with disability.

step_free_access.description: True when the features recorded as yes or limited can be reached from arrival without steps.

hearing_loop.description: True when reception or the main building has a hearing loop.

FerryServiceAccessibility.description: Access for people with disability on a ferry service. boarding covers getting on and off with the ferry terminal ramp or gangway, and seating the passenger areas. Access at the ferry terminals themselves is recorded on the terminal sites. A change that raises access to yes goes to a person (the accessibility_raised fixed check), because a wrong yes can strand a traveller who relied on it.

wheelchair.description: Wheelchair access to each feature of the ferry service. A feature that is absent is unknown.

step_free_access.description: True when a wheelchair user can board and reach the passenger areas without steps.

hearing_loop.description: True when the passenger areas have a hearing loop.

Contact.description: Public contact details of the site's operator. Never a contributor's personal details.

Capacity.description: How many vehicles or groups the site holds.

StayLimits.description: Limits on how long a traveller may stay.

period_days.description: The period over which max_nights applies, for example 2 nights in any 28 days.

VehicleLengthM.description: A vehicle or rig length in metres.

VehicleHeightM.description: A vehicle height or vertical clearance in metres, from the road surface. Capped at 10 m, so a figure in feet such as 13.5 fails instead of passing as metres.

VehicleWidthM.description: A vehicle width or width limit in metres. Capped at 10 m, so a figure in feet fails instead of passing as metres.

HeadingDeg.description: A compass heading of travel in degrees from true north, 0 up to but not including 360.

LineGeometry.description: The line a road segment or ferry service follows: a GeoJSON LineString or MultiLineString (RFC 7946) in WGS84. Positions run in the order a traveller would follow them from the start of the record, and the direction carries no meaning unless a fact says so.

Road.description: The road a road restriction is on or a road segment is part of, as signposted.

name.description: The road's name, for example Princes Highway or Wonnangatta Track.

ref.description: The route number shown on signs, for example A1, B500 or C142.

Structure.description: The built thing at a road restriction, from the structure governed list (structures.json), and how the road passes it. passage over: the vehicle drives on or across it, so weight and width matter (a bridge carrying the road, a causeway). under: the vehicle passes beneath it, so vertical clearance matters (a rail bridge over the road, a sign gantry). through: the vehicle passes through it (a tunnel, a gate, a ford). along: a limit signed on the open road. Each structure code lists the passages it allows.

LimitBasis.description: What a limit figure is. signed: the figure on the sign, the legal limit, which usually allows a margin. surveyed: measured by the road authority or a surveyor, often with a survey certificate. measured: measured by a contributor, for example with a tape or a height pole. unknown: the source does not say. Open: a consumer treats a basis it does not know as unknown, and still compares a rig with lowest_m.

LimitMeasurement.description: One figure for a vertical clearance or width limit, in metres. A structure can have several: a signed and a surveyed figure, one per direction of travel, or one per lane.

value_m.description: The figure in metres. The fact that holds the measurement sets its range: VehicleHeightM for vertical clearance and VehicleWidthM for width limit, both capped at 10 m.

heading_deg.description: The heading of travel this figure applies to. Absent when it applies in every direction.

lane.description: The lane this figure applies to, as the source names it, for example 1, 2 or kerb. Absent when it applies across the road.

observed_on.description: When the figure was signed, surveyed or measured, if the source says.

certificate_url.description: A survey certificate for a surveyed figure.

MeasuredLimit.description: The shape shared by vertical clearance and width limit: every figure known, signed, surveyed or measured, and the lowest of them. The fact that uses it sets the range of lowest_m and of each figure's value_m.

lowest_m.description: The lowest figure of any basis in measurements, in metres. Rig filters and apps compare a vehicle with this figure, never with the signed figure alone, because a measured or surveyed figure lower than the sign is the one that strikes the vehicle.

lowest_basis.description: The basis of the lowest figure, so an app can say whether it is the signed limit or a lower measured or surveyed one.

VerticalClearance.description: Safety fact. The height a vehicle must be under to pass, in metres. measurements holds every figure known, signed, surveyed or measured, and lowest_m is the lowest of them, whatever its basis. That is the figure every rig filter compares a vehicle with.

WidthLimit.description: Safety fact. The width a vehicle must be under to pass, in metres, such as a single-lane bridge or a gate. lowest_m is the lowest figure of any basis, as for vertical clearance.

WeightLimit.description: Safety fact. The signed mass limits, in tonnes. gross_t is the gross mass of the vehicle or combination, including anything towed. axle_load_t is the most any one axle may carry. Either or both may be given.

axle_load_t.description: Most mass any one axle may carry, in tonnes.

assessed_on.description: When the road authority last assessed the limit, if the source says.

LengthLimit.description: Safety fact. The longest vehicle or combination allowed, as signed, in metres.

Surface.description: What a road segment is made of, from the surface governed list (surfaces.json), and how rough it is. condition is how the surface rides at the time observed: good, fair (some potholes or corrugations, normal speeds with care), poor (slow going for any vehicle), very_poor (high clearance needed) or impassable.

VehicleAccessClass.description: Safety fact. The least capable vehicle that can use a road segment, from the vehicle access class governed list (vehicle-access-classes.json).

TowingPermitted.description: Safety fact. Whether vehicles may tow a trailer, caravan or camper trailer. yes: towing allowed. not_recommended: allowed, but the land manager or road authority advises against it. no: towing prohibited. It comes from contributors, who can add a photo of the sign, and a seed source never sets it.

SeasonalClosure.description: Safety fact. When a road segment or ferry service closes every year or after weather, and the authority that closes it. Declared closures change daily and are never stored: apps send travellers to info_url for current conditions. The periods are local calendar days, read in the record's time zone or in time_zone when it is given. authority is the authority that declares closures, and info_url its official page for current closures and conditions

periods.description: Periods it closes every year, such as a winter closure of a high country track.

dates_year.description: The year whose published dates the periods were taken from. Authorities set the exact dates each year, so apps show the periods as typical and link to info_url.

wet_weather_closure.description: True when it closes, or becomes impassable, after rain or in floods.

Terminals.description: The two ferry terminals a ferry service runs between: sites whose site types include ferry_terminal. A service that calls at more places is recorded as one ferry service per crossing.

Operator.description: The operator of a ferry service: the organisation that runs it, with its public contact details.

AcceptedVehicleClasses.description: Safety fact. The vehicle classes a ferry service carries, from the vehicle class governed list (vehicle-classes.json). A class not listed is not carried, so this decides whether a car towing a caravan may board.

FerryVehicleLimits.description: Safety fact. The ferry vehicle limits: the largest vehicle a ferry service carries, the ferry's counterpart of a site's rig limits. The top-level limits apply to every vehicle. by_vehicle_class gives tighter limits for one class, such as a shorter maximum for a car towing a caravan. Lengths are the combined length of the vehicle and anything it tows, including the drawbar. max_total_load_t is the most the ferry carries on one crossing. A limit that is absent is unknown, not unlimited.

max_total_load_t.description: Most total mass on one crossing, in tonnes.

Fares.description: What a crossing costs, by vehicle class. charging says whether there is a charge at all. items lists the fares.

time_zone.description: The zone the season, valid_from and valid_to in the fares' conditions are read in, when it is not the record's time_zone.

charging.description: free: no charge, as on many council river ferries. paid: a fare applies and items lists it.

FareItem.description: One fare: the price for one vehicle of a vehicle class, or one foot passenger, for one crossing or a return crossing. Operators usually price vehicles in length bands, and sometimes height bands, which band gives.

crossings.description: 1 for a one-way fare, 2 for a return fare.

VehicleBand.description: A range of vehicle sizes a fare covers, such as a car over 5.5 m or a car towing a caravan from 6 m to 13 m. Lengths are combined, including the drawbar and anything towed. A minimum is exclusive and a maximum inclusive, so bands that meet at 5.5 m do not overlap.

Crossing.description: How a ferry service runs. departures: on_demand (the ferry crosses when vehicles arrive, as small river ferries do), continuous (it shuttles back and forth without a timetable) or timetabled (fixed departure times, published at timetable_url). duration_minutes is the usual time on the water.

capacity_cars.description: How many cars the ferry carries on one crossing, as operators of small vehicle ferries publish it.

FacilityValue.description: Whether a site has a facility, and its attributes. available false records that the facility is known to be absent, which is different from the facility being missing from the record (unknown). The attributes allowed for each code are listed in facilities.json and checked by the per-code schemas in this file.

Facilities.description: A map from facility code to facility value. Codes with defined attributes are checked here. Codes not listed are accepted with free-form attributes so that new governed list entries do not break older validators. In stored sites and in submissions the codes facilities.json marks with stored_as are read from other facts instead (see StoredFacilities). The compact site form fills them in for convenience.

StoredFacilities.description: Facilities as submitted and stored: the codes read from other facts are not allowed. The anyOf lists exactly the codes facilities.json marks with stored_as, and tools/validate.py checks that the two agree.

FacilityWithAttributes.description: Helper: a facility value whose attributes object is replaced by a per-code schema.

fee.description: True when the showers cost extra (coins, tokens or a separate charge).

potable.description: True when signed or known to be safe to drink without treatment.

treated.description: True when the supply is treated (chlorinated, filtered or UV).

tank_fill.description: True when a hose or tap allows filling a vehicle's water tank.

amps.description: Rated current per outlet, in amperes.

outlets.description: Number of outlets available to travellers.

metered.description: True when use is metered and charged by consumption.

outlet_type.description: The socket standard as written on the outlet, for example AS/NZS 3112 15 A.

guests_only.description: True when only paying guests may use it.

FiresAllowedValue.description: Safety fact. The site's standing policy on campfires. Total fire bans and other bans declared by fire authorities always override it and are not recorded in OTWD.

MobileCoverageValue.description: Mobile coverage as contributors observed it on site, by carrier. These are observations, not carrier coverage maps. available false means no carrier had any signal when observed.

carrier.description: The network the device was on, as the device named it.

AccessibleFacilitiesValue.description: Read from the accessibility fact, and absent when no wheelchair feature is recorded. available is false, with no attributes, when arrival is no or every recorded feature is no. Otherwise available is true, and wheelchair is yes when arrival is yes and every recorded feature is yes, and limited in every other case: arrival limited, any feature limited or no, or arrival not recorded, since an unknown arrival gives limited at best. features lists the features whose access is yes.

CountedValue.description: A facility whose only attribute is how many there are.
